_comment: Two engines find the same thing and call it different names. gitleaks
writes private-key, trufflehog writes PrivateKey, and semgrep writes
detected-jwt-token for what gitleaks calls jwt. Deduplication is not the
problem: a credential is keyed on the hash of its value, so the same
secret found twice is already one finding. The problem is that a rule
level exclusion or a severity override has to be written twice, and
whoever writes one believes they are covered.
Most of it needs no table. A name is squashed to letters and digits and
compared, so PrivateKey and private-key are already the same key and both
come out as private-key. This file is only for the pairs where the two
engines genuinely used different words, and for acronyms the camel case
The key is the name with everything but letters and digits removed, in
lower case. The value is the name to use.
